newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australians think immigration too high - poll.
newsitem.headline: Australians think immigration too high - poll.

text.p: More than seven out of 10 Australian voters believe immigration levels are too high despite a government plan for further cuts, according to a newspaper poll published on Friday.

The Newspoll survey, reflecting a national debate prompted by anti-immigration remarks by an independent member of parliament, also showed that 52 percent of the voters believed immigration was "a lot too high."
The survey, published in The Australian newspaper, showed feelings against immigrants running highest among older people and those on low incomes.
A total of 71 percent of 1,200 voters polled by telephone last week said that immigration levels were "a lot too high" or a "little too high."
Only two percent thought them too low, while 20 percent judged them to be about right. Seven percent were undecided.
The poll follows widespread media coverage of a maiden parliamentary speech on September 10 by Pauline Hanson, who said the country was in danger of being swamped by Asians.
Hanson called for an immediate halt to immigration and said Australia's policy of "multi-culturalism," introduced in the 1970s after decades of whites-only immigration, should be ditched.
Australia's conservative government said in July it would cut general immigration by almost 11 percent to 74,000 in the current fiscal year to June 30, 1997.

Responding to unemployment problems, the government said it would select migrants with better English language and work skills who could contribute more quickly to national wealth. But it said its immigration policy would remain non-discriminatory.
